transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. 

I just came in because... well, my sleep has been all broken up lately. I mean, I work overnight shifts as a personal care aide, so I know my schedule is already kind of weird, but I'll get off my shift and still just lie there wide awake in bed. And then, when I finally do drift off, I just... I wake up really scared. I feel like I never rested at all. 

Is that... does that make sense as a reason to be here? I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to get it checked out.
When you wake up feeling scared after falling asleep, do you remember having a bad dream or nightmare?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really remember any dreams at all, bad or otherwise. I just... I wake up and my heart is racing, and I feel this sort of panic, but I couldn't tell you why. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I know it would probably be more helpful if I could point to a specific nightmare or something, but it's really just this overwhelming feeling of being scared for no reason. Is that... is that normal for someone with sleep issues?
Have you ever experienced a moment where you're waking up and you can't move your body at all, like you're paralyzed?

No, no, I've never had anything like that. I can always move just fine. I mean, I might just lie there because I'm so tired, but I'm definitely not paralyzed or anything scary like that. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I'm just having a little trouble sleeping, that's all. I haven't had any of that paralysis stuff. Does that... does that help rule things out for you?
Do you find yourself having trouble turning off your thoughts or feeling worried when you're trying to fall asleep?

Um, well... I guess I do think a lot, but I wouldn't say I'm, like, overly worried or anything. It's just normal stuff, you know? Like, did I do everything right at work, or... did I forget to lock the door. Just little things. 

I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining or like I can't handle my own thoughts. Everyone gets a little wound up sometimes, right? I just try to focus on being a good worker and getting through the night. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the right information.
Do you find yourself feeling very sleepy or tired during the day, even after you’ve had some sleep?

Um, no, not really. I mean, maybe just a normal amount? Since I work as a personal care aide, I'm on my feet helping people a lot, so... so I might get a little worn out by the afternoon. But I definitely don't fall asleep during the day or anything bad like that. 

I really don't want you to think I'm lazy or that I can't handle my job. I always make sure to push through and take good care of my clients, no matter what. I just drink a little coffee and I'm totally fine. 

Is it okay that I don't have that happening? I hope I'm still being helpful with all this... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers for your notes.
Do you ever feel like your sleep is restless, or that you're not getting good quality rest even if you're not waking up completely during the night?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I think that's actually why I finally came in, just because my sleep has been getting kind of... broken up lately. Like, I'll get off an overnight shift with my clients, and I know I should just go right to sleep, but I end up just lying there wide awake. And then when I do finally manage to drift off, I've been waking up feeling kind of scared, and it just feels like I never rested at all. 

But I'm sure it's just because of my weird work schedule, right? Working overnights is hard on anybody, so it's probably normal to get a little mixed up. I really don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know I just need to push through it and do my job. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
Can you tell me more about the broken-up sleep you mentioned? How often do you wake up during the night, and how long do these awakenings usually last?

Um, gosh, I actually... I don't really know for sure. I'm sorry. I try really hard not to look at the clock when it happens, just because I don't want to stress myself out and make it worse, you know? 

I don't think it's a lot, though! I just kind of toss and turn a little bit. And I don't think I'm awake for very long, honestly. I just try to force myself to stay in bed and close my eyes so I can be ready for my clients the next day. I really try not to let it be a big deal.

I'm really sorry I don't have exact numbers or times for you. Is it okay that I don't really keep track? I can definitely start writing it down if that would help you more! I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Is your sleep being interrupted by things like phone calls, alarms, or other noises related to your job or environment while you're trying to rest?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. Um, I always make sure my phone is on silent, and my room is pretty quiet. I live in a nice, quiet spot, so it's not like traffic or neighbors or anything waking me up. 

I mean, I really try to set myself up for a good sleep so I can be at my best for work. I don't let distractions get in the way. It's just... it's just me waking up on my own, I guess. 

Is that what you meant? I hope I'm not doing something wrong with my routine... I can try to make it even quieter if you think that would help! I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to.
Have you ever experienced any sudden muscle weakness or loss of muscle control, especially during the day while you're awake?

Um, muscle weakness? Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I'm on my feet a lot for work, helping my clients move around and everything, so I really have to stay strong for them. I've never just... lost control of my muscles or anything like that. 

I might get a little tired sometimes, but that's just normal fatigue from working hard, right? Nothing sudden or scary like you're talking about. I always make sure I can do my job properly. 

Is that... is that a good thing? I hope that's the right answer. I'm trying really hard to give you the information you need.
Do you ever notice yourself snoring loudly or having trouble breathing during sleep?

Oh, no, I don't think so. Um, I sleep by myself, so I guess I wouldn't have anyone to tell me if I was snoring, but I've never woken myself up doing it or anything like that. And I've never woken up gasping for air or feeling like I couldn't breathe. 

I really try to take good care of my health so I can be there for my clients. I know sleep apnea and things like that can be really bad for you, so I'd definitely tell you if I thought I had that! 

I'm pretty sure my breathing is totally normal at night. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt awake but couldn’t move your body, either when falling asleep or right after waking up?

Um, not being able to move? Oh, no, I've never had anything like that happen. I always wake up and get right out of bed, you know, to get ready for the day. 

I mean, sometimes it's a little hard to find the energy to get going, but my body always works just fine. I definitely wouldn't want to be stuck like that, especially since I need to be reliable for the people I take care of. 

I've never been paralyzed or anything... that sounds really frightening. I hope it's okay that I haven't experienced that. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can help me.
When you're falling asleep or waking up, have you ever seen, heard, or felt things that weren't actually there?

Um, seeing or hearing things? No, not when I'm waking up or falling asleep. I mean, sometimes when I'm just lying there, my mind wanders a bit, but that's just normal dreaming or, you know, just thoughts before sleep. 

I've never had any weird hallucinations or anything scary like that in bed. I always make sure my bedroom is nice and quiet so I can get proper rest for work. I know how important a good night's sleep is.

So, no, nothing like that. Is that... is that what you were looking for? I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you.
Do you ever feel an uncomfortable sensation in your legs or an urge to move them when you're trying to fall asleep or resting?

Um, an uncomfortable feeling in my legs? No, I don't think so. I mean, sometimes my feet get a little tired after being on them all day with my clients, but that's just normal soreness, right? 

I don't get any weird urges to move them or anything when I'm trying to rest. I usually just try to lay still and go to sleep so I can be rested for the next day. I wouldn't want anything keeping me awake when I need to be alert for work. 

So, no, my legs are fine. I hope that's a good thing? I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
How long does it usually take you to fall asleep after you get into bed?

Um, well... lately it takes me a really long time. I know I should be sleeping better, especially since I work overnight shifts sometimes. I want to be well-rested, I really do try. 

But I'll get off an overnight shift, and I'll just lie there in bed, wide awake for hours. It's like my sleep is just... all broken up now. And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I wake up feeling really scared. And I feel like I haven't rested at all. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be doing a better job at managing my sleep schedule. Is it normal to struggle this much with sleeping after night shifts? I hope I'm not doing something wrong.
Do you usually have trouble falling asleep within a reasonable amount of time when you first go to bed?

Um, yes... I think I just mentioned that, actually. I'm sorry if I didn't explain it well enough the first time. 

But yes, it takes me a very long time. Like I said, I'll get off my overnight shift and I just... I lie there wide awake. For hours, sometimes. I know I should be able to just close my eyes and sleep, especially when I'm so tired, but my sleep is just all broken up now. 

And then when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up feeling really scared, and it's like I never rested at all. I really am trying my best to get on a normal schedule, I promise. I just... I can't seem to do it right now. Is that okay? I mean, does that make sense for what you're asking?
Can you tell me how long, on average, it takes you to fall asleep after you first lie down for the night?

Um, well... like I was saying, it just takes hours. I don't really have an exact number, I'm sorry. I try not to look at the clock because I know I'll just get more stressed about not sleeping, and I want to do everything I can to relax. 

If I had to guess, maybe... two or three hours? Sometimes more? I just lie there, trying so hard to be still and let it happen. I really am trying to do the right things to get enough rest for my clients. I hope it's not too frustrating that I can't give you an exact number of minutes. I can start keeping a journal if that would be more helpful for you?
Do you consistently have trouble falling asleep within 30 minutes of lying down, or does it sometimes take even longer?

Um, yes, it's... it's definitely longer than 30 minutes. Like I mentioned, it's usually hours of just lying there wide awake after my overnight shift. 

I'm really sorry to keep repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. I came in today specifically because my sleep is just all broken up now. I try so hard to get a good day's sleep after my shift, but I just can't. And then when I finally do drift off, I wake up feeling so scared, and it's like I never rested at all. 

I hope I'm giving you the information you need. I know it's probably frustrating to deal with someone who can't even manage a normal sleep schedule. Is it okay that it takes me that long? I'm really trying my best to fix it.
Is it only after your overnight shifts that you have trouble falling asleep, or do you also have difficulty falling asleep at other times when you're not working nights?

Oh, um, I'm sorry if I made it sound like it was only after work. I didn't mean to be confusing. It's... it's really anytime I try to sleep now. Even on my nights off, I still just lie there wide awake. 

Like I mentioned before, that's really the main reason I came in, just because my sleep is so broken up across the board. And no matter what day it is, when I do finally manage to drift off, I still wake up feeling so scared... and it just feels like I never rested at all. I try so hard to catch up on my days off so I can be at my best, I really do. 

I hope I'm explaining this okay for you. Does that make sense for what you needed to know?
Do you often wake up much earlier than you intended and find it difficult to fall back asleep?

Um, yes... I do. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just saying the same things over and over to you, but that's exactly what I meant when I said my sleep is all broken up now. 

When I finally do drift off, I'll just suddenly wake up way before I'm supposed to. And like I mentioned, I wake up feeling so scared... and once that happens, I just can't get back to sleep no matter what I do. I just lie there feeling like I never rested at all. 

I promise I try really hard to force myself back to sleep, because I know I need to be alert and do a good job for my clients, but it just doesn't work. Is that what you were asking about? I really hope I'm not complaining too much, I just want to make sure you have all the right details.
